Russia won the war of 1877-78. Then the great powers met in Berlin and rewrote the peace in a month. This is the map of Europe they left behind.

a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ In March 1878 the Treaty of San Stefano created a large, Russian-backed Bulgaria with access to the Aegean. Britain and Austria-Hungary objected, and Bismarck hosted a congress in Berlin from 13 June to 13 July 1878 to revise it.

2/ Bulgaria was cut to less than half of the San Stefano plan. The north became a self-governing principality under the sultan. The south, Eastern Rumelia on the map, became an autonomous Ottoman province. Macedonia went back to the Ottomans.

3/ Romania, Serbia and Montenegro were recognised as fully independent. Romania had to give southern Bessarabia to Russia, its own wartime ally, and got Northern Dobruja in exchange. Relations stayed cold for decades.

4/ The biggest winners hadn't fought at all. Austria-Hungary got to occupy and run Bosnia-Herzegovina, then annexed it in 1908. Britain took over Cyprus through a secret deal with the Ottomans signed on 4 June, nine days before the congress opened.

5/ Eastern Rumelia lasted only seven years. A bloodless coup on 6 September 1885 joined it to Bulgaria, and Unification Day is still a national holiday there. Bosnia became the source of tensions that ended in Sarajevo in 1914.
A peace that held for a generation, or the first draft of 1914? How do you read the Berlin settlement? Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
